newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Rabin's killer allowed stereo for Bible lessons.
newsitem.headline: Rabin's killer allowed stereo for Bible lessons.

text.p: An Israeli court ruled on Sunday convicted Yitzhak Rabin assassin Yigal Amir can listen to Bible lessons on a personal stereo in his cell but rejected the killer's requests for easier prison conditions.

"I finished my function with the act I committed and now I want to sit and study and I have no intention to incite anyone," Amir, who killed Prime Minister Rabin at a Tel Aviv peace rally in November, 1995, was quoted by Israel's Itim news agency as telling the court.
Amir, a right-wing religious Jew, gunned down the Nobel peace laureate to stop Rabin from handing to the Palestinians West Bank lands which he believed God had promised to the Jews.

Itim said the court rejected Amir's requests to be moved to a prison closer to his family, to be allowed more telephone and visiting privileges, to bring additional books into his cell and to remove television cameras he said invaded his privacy.
"Amir does not deserve additional privileges because his behaviour has not been good, including hunger strikes and attempts to cover camera lenses in his cell," Itim said the court had ruled.

Itim said the court decided the right-wing religious assassin would be allowed to bring a personal stereo into his cell to listen to Bible lessons. It also ruled Amir could have his hair cut and his clothes and bedding laundered more often.

The court also said a prison commission could decide whether to grant Amir his request to bring a personal computer into his cell in order to finish a computer degree. The court recommended Amir be allowed the computer only if it were gutted to prevent its use as a communications device.
Amir, 26, was sentenced to life in prison plus six years for assassinating Rabin and wounding his bodyguard. he received an additional seven years in a separate conspiracy trial.
